dish.title: Cambodian Fish Amok: Steamed Coconut-Lemongrass Fish Custards with Jasmine Rice

Topped with a spoonful of the thick coconut milk, slivered lime leaf, and chile, with jasmine rice.

recipe_version.title: Cambodian Fish Amok: Steamed Coconut-Lemongrass Fish Custards with Jasmine Rice
recipe_version.description: Chunks of white fish folded into a custard of coconut milk, eggs, fish sauce, and a fresh kroeung paste of lemongrass, ginger, turmeric, garlic, shallot, lime leaves, and red chile, steamed in spinach-lined ramekins until just firm. Topped with a spoonful of the thick coconut milk, slivered lime leaf, and chile, with jasmine rice.

ingredients.name: cod or other firm white fish
ingredients.display_name: skinless cod or other firm white fish

ingredients.name: lemongrass
ingredients.preparation: tender lower 5 inches only, thinly sliced

ingredients.name: makrut lime leaves
ingredients.preparation: center ribs removed; 3 for the paste, 1 slivered to garnish

ingredients.name: red chile (Fresno)
ingredients.preparation: half chopped for the paste, half thinly sliced to garnish

ingredients.name: full-fat coconut milk
ingredients.note: 1/4 cup thick cream reserved for topping

ingredients.name: fish sauce
ingredients.display_name: fish sauce (anchovy and salt; label lists no shrimp or shellfish)

steps.title: Prep
steps.body: Trim the lemongrass to the tender lower 5 inches and slice it thin. Slice the ginger, peel the garlic, and chop the shallots. Strip the ribs from the lime leaves; sliver 1 leaf very fine. Chop half the chile and thinly slice the rest. Cut the fish into 1-inch chunks. Rinse the rice.

steps.title: Make the kroeung
steps.body: Spoon off 1/4 cup of the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk and set it aside. In a food processor grind the lemongrass, ginger, turmeric, garlic, shallots, 3 lime leaves, and the chopped chile with 1/4 cup of the remaining coconut milk to a fine paste, scraping down often, about 4 minutes.

steps.title: Mix and fill
steps.body: In a mixing bowl whisk the rest of the coconut milk, the eggs, fish sauce, brown sugar, and the kroeung. Fold in the fish. Line 6 ramekins with the spinach and divide the fish mixture among them, a scant 1 cup each, so each is about three-quarters full. Set 3 ramekins in each tier of the bamboo steamer.

steps.title: Steam the custards
steps.body: Put 4 cups water in a 14-inch wok (6-quart), cover, and bring to a boil over high, about 6 minutes to come to a boil; it must sit below the base of the bamboo steamer. While it heats, start the rice: combine the rice, 2 1/4 cups water, and 1/2 tsp salt in a 2-quart saucepan, bring to a boil over high, about 4 minutes, cover, cook on low 15 minutes, then leave it covered off the heat 10 minutes (overlap stated). Set the stacked two-tier steamer in the wok, cover with its lid, and steam over medium, swapping the tiers after 11 minutes, until the custard no longer jiggles at the center and the fish reaches 145 F, about 22 minutes. Spoon the reserved coconut cream over the six custards, about 2 tsp each, and steam 1 minute more.

steps.title: Serve
steps.body: Lift out the ramekins with tongs, top with the slivered lime leaf and sliced chile, and serve with the rice, 1 or 2 ramekins per person.

equipment: 14-inch flat-bottomed wok (6-quart) that the steamer sits in

scaling_notes.1: A quarter of everything in 2 (10-ounce) ramekins, each about half full, in one tier of the bamboo steamer over the wok; start checking at 16 minutes. A quarter of the rice in a 1-quart saucepan.
scaling_notes.2: Half of everything in 3 (10-ounce) ramekins, three-quarters full, in one tier of the bamboo steamer; about 22 minutes, no tier swap. Half the rice in a 1-quart saucepan.
scaling_notes.4: As written (6 ramekins, three per tier, two tiers).
do_not_scale: fill: each 10-ounce ramekin about three-quarters full (a scant 1 cup of mix) so the custard can puff; use more ramekins, not fuller ones
steaming time: about 22 minutes for three-quarters-full 10-ounce ramekins; with both tiers in use, swap them halfway

coverage_contribution: Cambodia has no meal in the catalog, and nothing is steamed in ramekins. An HH001 fish dinner with an easy, hands-off steaming step.
near_duplicate_review: Compared with thai-fish-cakes-cucumber-relish: a soft steamed coconut custard with fish chunks, not fried fish cakes. Compared with brazilian-fish-moqueca: steamed and set with egg, not a stew. Compared with ginger-scallion-fish-packets: fish in a lemongrass-coconut custard in ramekins, not steamed in packets with ginger and scallion. Compared with thai-red-curry-kabocha: a fresh herb paste set into a custard, not a curry-paste stew.
not_duplicate_of: Not served in banana-leaf cups; ramekins keep it practical.
